title: Exercise in Nature Improves Performance and Mood
paragraphs: Spending time in nature is good for your mind. But according to a new study from the UK, it may also help your body perform better during exercise.
The study was carried out by researchers at Loughborough University and led by Dr. Danny Longman. It was published in the American Journal of Biological Anthropology in 2026.

The study involved 25 healthy adults. Each person took part in the experiment twice. One time, they spent 90 minutes in an ancient woodland. Another time, they spent 90 minutes in an urban industrial area. After each visit, they did a cycling test in a laboratory. They had to cycle until they were too tired to continue.

The results showed that the participants' endurance was 7.5% better after they visited the woodland. On average, they were able to cycle about 1.1 minutes longer. In addition, the participants' mood improved a lot after the woodland visit, and this lasted for up to two hours. They also felt more optimistic. The researchers believe that these psychological effects may partly explain why the participants performed better.

According to Longman, the results show that nature does not only help people relax. It also actively supports the way the human body works. He believes this means that green spaces may be more important for physical health than people think.
However, the study was small, with only 25 people, so more research is needed.
Other research has found similar results. A 2025 study from Denmark found that walking in nature reduced stress more than walking in a city or indoors.
